newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek rates surge, bonds bleed on drachma softness.
newsitem.headline: Greek rates surge, bonds bleed on drachma softness.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards soared by up to one percentage point -- to 12.90 percent in periods up to three-months, and to 11.30 percent from there to one-year -- on tighter liquidity linked to Tuesday's auction of bonds and today's forex outflows, dealers said.
Short-term rates could rise further should the central bank indicate in the next few days that its intervention offer rate would be above 12.90 percent, dealers said.

"If liquidity calculations are correct, we might have a liquidity shortage in the next couple of days and rates could go as high as the lombard, currently at 19 percent," said a dealer at another foreign bank.
Dealers agreed that the central bank's move to leave more liquidity into the system would do little to relieve the cash hungry market.

The drachma recovered some ground against the ecu after the central bank's intervention at the fixing where it sold about $60 million and 660 million ecus to prop up the drachma, dealers said. Ecu/drachma was trading around 309.90 in late dealings.
Bonds and FRNs which shed 30 to 50 basis points in terms of price continued to be soft and dealers said they were adversely affected by higher interbank rates.

"The market is cash strapped, pulling depos and implied drachma rates from forex forwards up," said a senior money market dealer at a foreign bank. "Rates are trading around 12.90 percent in tenors up to three-months and 11.30 percent in the rest of the curve."

The Bank of Greece drained 50 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular depo tender on Wednesday. A facility of 100 billion drachmas was expiring today, boosting the system's liquidity by about 50 billion drachmas.
Dealers blamed the tighter liquidity conditions on Tuesday's bond auction and today's forex outflows.

"In my view, the shortage is forex spot driven," said the senior money market dealer. "To be more specific, it relates to speculation that the dollar will continue to be robust against EMS currencies and the drachma."
He added that speculators did not care much about paying the points or the opportunity cost involved when they expected huge profits from a favourable move in dollar/drachma.
Ecu/drachma was hovering below 310, currently trading around 309.90, and dealers said ecu selling by locals helped the cross soften after the central bank's fixing.
Bonds and FRNs continued to exhibit weakness after coming under pressure earlier in the day.

"I think we will keep on watching the same movie til September," said a senior bond dealer at a foreign bank. "I just hope that the finance ministry will leave plenty of money in the system in September when a huge amount of treasuries matures."
In addition to the higher cost of interbank funding, part of today's bond decline was explained by the correction of price misalignments arising from yesterday's auction, the dealer said.
Greece sought bids for 75 billion drachmas each of five- and seven-year bonds with coupons of 9.2 percent and 8.9 percent respectively, and 120 billion drachmas of 8.8 percent, 10-year bonds.
The five- and seven-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on March 19 and then bids were re-opened on June 17. The 10-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on June 17.
Greece will also auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes on July 29.
Bids totalling 167 billion drachmas, 123 billion and 233 billion respectively were submitted for five-, seven- and 10-year bonds at the auction.
The mark was quoted at 156.93/03 from Wednesday's 156.990 fix, the dollar at 281.22/32 drachmas from 281.500 and the ecu at 309.77/87 from 309.92 drachmas.
